findings.text: VIX closed at 24.35 on 2026-11-06: Elevated regime, backwardation (VIX / VIX3M = 1.027).
Markov chain from today: 34% chance of a Crisis day within 1 month, 93% within 12 (historical frequency from this regime: 37% and 84%).
VIX forecasts risk: correlation with next-month realized SPY vol is 0.60; VIX exceeded subsequent realized vol on 84% of days (the volatility risk premium).
VIX does not reliably forecast direction: after Crisis closes, next-month SPY averaged +3.9% (t = 2.26, 8 months). Selling on VIX spikes tends to sell near lows.
VIXY (long VIX futures) returned -99.8% over the regime window: futures roll decay makes a permanent VIX hedge expensive.
A 5% VIXY sleeve on Max Sharpe cuts Crisis-regime vol from 26.1% to 21.3% and costs 2.48% a year in expected return.
Maximum Sharpe Ratio: best VIX rule (Term-structure switch) did not improve Sharpe (0.85 static vs 0.82); max drawdown -17.6% vs -19.7%.
Minimum Variance: best VIX rule (Regime map) improved Sharpe (0.28 static vs 0.31); max drawdown -24.1% vs -19.9%.
VIX Crisis-Constrained: best VIX rule (Regime map) did not improve Sharpe (0.67 static vs 0.63); max drawdown -17.9% vs -17.0%.
SPY only: best VIX rule (Term-structure switch) improved Sharpe (0.73 static vs 0.79); max drawdown -33.7% vs -27.0%.

Workbook Spread Total vs next-week SPY return: correlation -0.096 (t = -2.18, 519 weeks), a weak but stable link (same sign in both halves: -0.072, -0.119); it explains about 0.9% of next-week SPY variance. VIX change alone shows +0.006, so any signal comes from the commodity and yield legs. Against next-week VIX change: -0.010 (t = -0.24).
Latest week (2026-11-06): Difference +5.30 pts, bucket '+3 and up'.
After Difference +3 and up, VIX was lower the next week 81% of the time (47 weeks; normal week 56%; halves 80% / 82%).
No non-VIX workbook series has a significant and stable edge there; the best is long DOW Jones Commodity at 57% vs 53% normally (p = 0.31).
After Difference +5 and up (extreme), VIX was lower the next week 75% of the time (24 weeks; normal week 56%; halves 73% / 78%).
In that bucket, workbook series with a significant and stable edge: short Oil (CL=F) won 67% vs 46% normally.
Daily, since 2010: after the VIX rose (Difference > 0) it was lower the next period 57% of the time (64% after a big rise, median -2.9%); after it fell, 53%. Rises revert, falls do not.
Weekly, since 2010: after the VIX rose (Difference > 0) it was lower the next period 64% of the time (75% after a big rise, median -8.1%); after it fell, 50%. Rises revert, falls do not.

Non-VIX instruments with a significant (|t| >= 2) and stable response after big VIX rises: UUP weekly +0.31% vs other periods (t = 2.7); IWM daily +0.21% vs other periods (t = 2.5); QQQ daily +0.17% vs other periods (t = 2.0).
Daily long SPY after big VIX rises: 424 trades, +0.17% per trade net of costs (vs +0.06% on an average period, t = 2.3), hit rate 56%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.59 vs 0.81 buy-and-hold.
Daily long QQQ after big VIX rises: 424 trades, +0.22% per trade net of costs (vs +0.08% on an average period, t = 2.5), hit rate 56%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.68 vs 0.88 buy-and-hold.
Daily long XLP after big VIX rises: 424 trades, +0.12% per trade net of costs (vs +0.05% on an average period, t = 2.3), hit rate 55%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.51 vs 0.71 buy-and-hold.

Weekly long UUP after big VIX rises: 84 trades, +0.24% per trade net of costs (vs +0.05% on an average period, t = 2.3), hit rate 58%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.49 vs 0.17 buy-and-hold (better).

Weekly short DJP after big VIX rises: 84 trades, +0.23% per trade net of costs (vs -0.03% on an average period, t = 1.3), hit rate 51%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.21 vs -0.19 always short (better).
Weekly long SPY after big VIX rises: 84 trades, +0.69% per trade net of costs (vs +0.27% on an average period, t = 1.5), hit rate 60%, in market 10% of the time; Sharpe 0.50 vs 0.78 buy-and-hold.
